source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-68: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 68 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Treat this as provisional RoCE diagnosis. Verify GPU/NIC and PCIe/NVLink topology, GPU-direct versus staging, firmware, drivers, library, MTU, link speed, VLAN/priority, PFC/ECN, route symmetry, queue pairs, registration, message sizes, concurrency, placement, clocks, and actual transport/fallback. Hypothesis: a priority or asymmetric-path mismatch amplified by congestion causes tail spikes; workload or host drift is the alternative. Start read-only. Capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency in ms, throughput, retries, timeouts, completion errors, NIC drops/ECN, switch queue/PFC counters, verbs requests/completions, and synchronized timestamps. Interleave fixed baseline/treatment with equal samples and uncertainty. Do not invent commands or expose credentials. An approved one-variable canary must have rollback and abort on preset p99.9 regression, correctness failure, timeout, drop, or pause increase.
